title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page. It is handwritten on the verso of an SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript page; the neighbouring pages are typescript pp. 80 and 127 of Exposé IX, which are unrelated to the content. The page belongs to the preparation of the divided-power de Rham complex lecture (IHES 1976).

Top part. There is a functor i: C → M, apparently M ↦ M ⊗_k S, where S = ⊕ S_i is a graded k-algebra, most likely a symmetric or divided-power algebra.
- There are truncation and shift operators τ_{N,0} and φ_{0,N}, with a natural transformation φ^{0,N}τ^{N,0}∘i → i.
- He gives an equalizer-type presentation M ↪ M^{[N,+∞[} ⇉ M^{[N,+∞[×ℕ}. The first map is x ↦ (c_{i,k−i} x)_{k≥N}. The two parallel maps send (x_k) to ε_{ℓ,k}x_k and c_{ℓ,k−i}x_{k+ℓ}.
- The structure constants c_{a,b} are presumably the multiplication constants of S, e.g. binomial coefficients γ_aγ_b = C(a+b,a)γ_{a+b} for divided powers. So M (sitting in degree i) is recovered as the subobject of sequences compatible with multiplication by S.
- He then considers the right-adjoint-type construction M ↦ Hom*_k(S,M) (graded Hom). He notes that the system (pro/ind-system) of Hom_k(S_i,M) compares with S ⊗_k M; for finite free modules the graded dual of Sym is Γ.
- He mentions Ab versus Ind(Ab): such limits/colimits may need to be taken in Ind-objects.
- He writes a map M ⊗_k S_i → Hom^i(τ_{N−i}(S), M ⊗_k S), i.e. a truncated version of the comparison.

Bottom part. A general definition. C is a k-linear category (i.e. a ring map k → End(id_C)), X an object of C, M a k-module.
- The cotensor Hom(M,X) ∈ C is defined by Hom(Y, Hom(M,X)) = Hom_k(M, Hom_C(Y,X)).
- The tensor M ⊗_k X is defined by Hom(M⊗_k X, Y) ≅ Hom_k(M, Hom_C(X,Y)).
- 'Dans la mesure où ça existe', M ↦ Hom(M,X) and M ↦ M ⊗_k X are 'exact à droite'.

These are the standard tensors/cotensors (copowers/powers) of a Mod_k-enriched category. They are used to make sense of M ⊗_k S and Hom(S,M) in a general k-linear category, as needed for divided-power/symmetric algebra constructions in an abstract abelian setting.
errors: The exactness statement is loose. M ↦ M⊗_k X is right exact, preserving colimits. M ↦ Hom(M,X) is contravariant: it sends cokernels to kernels, i.e. it is left exact in the usual sense (or 'right exact' only as a functor on Mod_k^op). The page's 'exact à droite' should be read as 'transforms colimits into limits'.
Hom_k(S_i,M) ≃ S⊗_k M in a 'system' sense requires finiteness/freeness of the S_i and an Ind/Pro interpretation; this is not stated.
The indexing in the equalizer formula is ambiguous ([N,+∞[ vs [N,+∞], ε_{ℓ,k} undefined), as expected in scratch.

ideas.what: Tensor and cotensor of objects of a k-linear category by k-modules, defined by representability
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly, Eilenberg–Kelly (enriched category theory, 1960s); folklore in SGA
ideas.where_published: similar constructions (M ⊗ X for module objects) appear implicitly in SGA 4 / SGA 3, unsure exact place

ideas.what: Presenting the image of M ↦ M⊗_k S (graded) by an equalizer of products using the multiplication constants of S; comparing with graded Hom*(S,M) and Ind-objects
ideas.modern_name: adjunction between M ↦ M⊗S and graded Hom(S,−); comodule/module duality Sym vs Γ

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scratch work: standard enriched tensor/cotensor definitions and a technical equalizer presentation for graded (likely divided-power) algebra modules. Nothing beyond standard material.
transcription_corrections: '𝒞 cat. de k-linéaire' should read '𝒞 cat. k-linéaire (i.e. k → End(id_𝒞))'.
'M un k-module t.f.[?]' is more plausibly 'M un k-module i.g. (supposé dans ...' — the handwriting is unclear.
The line 'i ⇒ φ_{0,N}τ_{N,0} ... i' contains a crossed-out symbol before i.
The last line reads '... est exact à droite' with 'à droite' partly obscured.
